title: Reading Drill — Monitoring visitors in a quiet reading room — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Monitoring visitors in a quiet reading room — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Bramley, work on people opening and closing heavy reference books abruptly had already produced a small collection of desk recordings. The reference librarian used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: brief peaks in background noise.

**B** The group kept padded book supports for the new trial, which was planned to run for eight weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that meetings in the next room should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
